title: Decision: what ADMIN, LUSERS and LINKS answer with
description:
ADMIN, LUSERS and LINKS are class 1 of epic mimid-1wgh.140: answerable from
the agent's own facts. Bead mimid-1wgh.140.1 implements them. Nine readings
had to be settled to write the three methods, all against
~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern.html, the Modern IRC Client Protocol,
and ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern-numerics.yml for every number.

259 RPL_ADMINEMAIL CARRIES A MIMI ADDRESS, AND MODERN'S MUST IS NOT MET.
Modern :3433 says <info> "MUST contain the email address to contact the
administrator(s) of the server". A mimid agent has no email address, and
nothing in the agent's store holds one.

Reading A: send the user's MIMI address, `<local>@<domain>`, which is
syntactically an address of that shape, is the real way to reach this
administrator (the agent's administrator is its own user), and is already
in every hostmask the client has seen.
Reading B: send nothing in 259, or omit 259, and fail Modern :1920's
SHOULD that an ADMIN reply carry all four numerics.

CHOSEN: A, with the parameter saying in the same breath that it is not an
email address. The MUST is unmet either way; A leaves the client something
true, B leaves a hole. No `wg` bead: Modern is not wrong here, mimid simply
has nothing the sentence asks for. The crate's `# Limitations` records the
unmet MUST where a reader looks for it.

THE PROSE OF 257, 258 AND 259 IS INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC. Modern says the
last parameter of all three "varies wildly" (:3415, :3424, :3433), so the
document fixes no text. The three sentences carry the three facts bead
mimid-1wgh.140.1 asks for, in its order: the user whose agent this is
(257, the numeric for the server's location), that the user runs it and
that the provider's domain serves the identity and not the agent (258,
whoever runs the server), and how to reach that administrator (259). The
tests assert all three by equality, so changing a word is one line in the
code and one in the test.

WHICH ADMIN TARGETS ARE ANSWERED. Modern :1914 answers a missing target
with this server's information, :1916 makes a target that names no server
here ERR_NOSUCHSERVER (402), and says that a target naming a client means
"the server that client is connected to".

CHOSEN: the reply goes out for no target, for `*`, for `[irc].server_name`
under eq_ignore_ascii_case, for the user's own nick and for the service
nick. Every other target is 402, the name echoed. The user's own nick and
the service nick are the only clients connected to this server; every
other nick and user URI the front end knows belongs to someone at a
provider, who is not connected here, so answering those with mimid's own
256 to 259 would assert something untrue about a peer's user. `Session::who`
is not consulted: it returns `Who::User` for any syntactically valid
`mimi://<domain>/u/<local>` whether the agent ever saw it, and its nick
lookup is the front end's shared `Names`, not this connection's channels.

AN EMPTY ADMIN PARAMETER IS NO TARGET. `ADMIN :` gives a target that is
given and names no server, which :1916 would answer 402 with the name
echoed -- but the name is empty, and an empty middle parameter cannot be
written: `Out::to_wire` prefixes `:` on the last parameter only, so the
line would go out with two spaces where the server name belongs and parse
as a different line. Readings: (a) treat it as no target and answer; (b)
402 with `*` or some other stand-in in place of the name the client sent.
CHOSEN: (a). (b) would name a server the client did not ask about. 461 is
not available: ADMIN's parameter is optional, and 461 is not in its reply
list (:1922-1938).

WILDCARDS OTHER THAN `*` ARE REFUSED. Modern :1918 says "Wildcards are
allowed in the <target> parameter", so `ADMIN mimid.*` should match
`mimid.invalid` and gets 402 instead. mimid matches no masks anywhere:
`ban_mode` (mimid-agent-irc/src/command.rs) refuses a mask rather than
matching one. A glob matcher would be the first on a socket input path in
this crate, and would need its own depth and backtracking limits under
AGENTS.md's named-limit rule. The literal `*` is matched because it names
the one server with no matcher. This is a declined permission, cited in
the code and in the crate's `# Limitations`.

251's <i> IS 1. Modern :3359 defines <u>, <i> and <s> as "the number of
total users, invisible users, and other servers connected to this server".
mimid answers `MODE <own nick>` with `221 +i` unconditionally and 004
advertises `i` as the one available user mode, so the user is invisible and
<i> is 1, not 0. <u> is 1 under Modern's word "total"; the common ircd
convention of sending visible users there (and meshIRCd's literal "0
invisible", main.go:1676) is not what this document says. <s> is 0 because
Modern says *other* servers; meshIRCd sends 1 in both 251 and 255, counting
itself, and a script written against it will read 0 here.

254 IS THE ASKING CONNECTION'S CHANNELS. Modern :3386 defines <channels>
as "the number of channels that currently exist on this server". On this
front end a channel exists exactly when a room the user is in has a channel
name, and `Names::note_room` gives a one-to-one room no channel name, so a
private query is not a channel that exists here. `self.channels.len()` is
that count as the asking connection has it, which is the set LIST walks and
which can lag the records by one change on a connection that has not caught
up with the feed. Not `state().rooms.len()`, which would count every
one-to-one room as a channel.

252, 253 AND 254 SEND 0 WHERE MODERN SAYS "POSITIVE INTEGER" (:3368, :3377,
:3386). Zero operators is what a server that answers OPER with 491 must
say (bead mimid-1wgh.140.2, decision mimid-1wgh.141); zero unknown
connections and zero channels are both ordinary states of a fresh agent.
251, 255, 265 and 266 say "non-negative" (:3359, :3395, :3451, :3462), so 0
needs no excuse there. Whether to raise the wording with ircdocs is Mark's
call, and would be a bead.

265 AND 266 ARE SENT, WITH THEIR TWO PARAMETERS. They are in LUSERS's
numeric list (:2002-2014) under the SHOULD at :1995, which covers 252, 253,
254, 265 and 266; 251 and 255 are that sentence's MUST. Modern :3453 and
:3464 make the two optional parameters a SHOULD of their own. Supplying
them costs one `peak_sessions` counter on the front end's `Shared`, raised
with `fetch_max` inside the registry's own lock. With no server link,
global equals local, so 266 repeats 265's numbers.

LINKS LISTS ONLY THIS SERVER. Modern :2878 requires zero or more 364 and
then one 365, and :2880 says "Servers MAY omit some or all servers on the
network, including itself", so one self-entry is a correct answer and not a
stub. Its shape is Modern's own reply example at :2896, where <server1> and
<server2> are the sending server and the hopcount is 0; the server info is
"mimid-agent", the string WHOIS 312 already sends. The provider and every
peer are left out: they are not IRC servers, and naming them would describe
mimid's topology to anything that asks (bead mimid-1wgh.140.1).

LUSERS AND LINKS IGNORE EVERY PARAMETER. Modern gives both "Parameters:
None" (:1990, :2873). RFC 2812 §3.4.2 (rfc2812.txt:1393) gives LUSERS
`[ <mask> [ <target> ] ]` and §3.4.5 (:1497) gives LINKS
`[ [ <remote server> ] <server mask> ]`; neither is Modern's command, so
neither 461 nor 402 is sent for a parameter, and the rustdocs cite Modern
and not the RFC.
